refund the $45.00 delivery fee

questions.stem: What is suggested about Ms. Lamarque?
options: She has previously bought furniture from Aldermoor.
She plans to order a replacement desk.
She assembled the desks with her own tools.
She bought the desks for members of her team.

fr.rule: Elle a choisi la livraison express « so that both desks would be here before our two new analysts join the team on April 21 » : les deux bureaux sont destinés aux nouveaux analystes de son équipe.

distractors.A: Aucun document ne parle d'un achat précédent.
distractors.B: Elle demande le remboursement du bureau abîmé et garde l'autre : elle ne parle pas de le remplacer.
distractors.C: Elle dit seulement avoir déballé les cartons (« unpacked »). La page précise que les outils sont fournis, et rien n'indique qu'elle ait utilisé les siens.

fr.trap: Pour une inférence sur une personne, cherche la raison qu'elle donne de son action : elle révèle souvent la situation (ici, équiper de nouveaux collègues).

en.rule: She chose express delivery "so that both desks would be here before our two new analysts join the team on April 21": the two desks are meant for the new analysts on her team.

distractors.A: No document mentions an earlier purchase.
distractors.B: She asks for a refund for the damaged desk and keeps the other: she does not mention replacing it.
distractors.C: She only says she unpacked the boxes ("unpacked"). The page says tools are included, and nothing shows she used her own.

en.trap: For an inference about a person, look for the reason she gives for her action: it often reveals the situation (here, equipping new colleagues).

evidence: so that both desks would be here before our two new analysts join the team on April 21

questions.stem: At 9:47 A.M., what does Ms. Mensah most likely mean when she writes, "Be my guest"?
options: She is inviting a visitor to the office.
She expects Mr. Tanaka to pay for the call.
She prefers to call the client herself.
She agrees that Mr. Tanaka should make the call.

fr.rule: « Be my guest » répond au message juste avant : M. Tanaka propose « I could call his office this morning if you like ». Mme Mensah accepte (« Be my guest », c'est « vas-y, je t'en prie ») et enchaîne avec des consignes pour l'appel : « Ask for his assistant, Ms. Reyes ».

distractors.A: Sens littéral de « guest » (invité) : personne n'est invité, il s'agit d'un appel téléphonique.
distractors.B: « Be my guest » peut évoquer « c'est moi qui invite », mais il n'est question d'aucun paiement ici.
distractors.C: Au contraire : elle laisse l'appel à M. Tanaka et lui dit qui demander.

fr.trap: Une réplique idiomatique répond au message d'avant : demande-toi ce qui vient d'être proposé, puis traduis par « j'accepte » ou « je refuse », jamais mot à mot.

en.rule: "Be my guest" answers the message just before: Mr. Tanaka offers "I could call his office this morning if you like". Ms. Mensah accepts ("Be my guest" means "go ahead") and then gives instructions for the call: "Ask for his assistant, Ms. Reyes".

distractors.A: The literal meaning of "guest": nobody is being invited anywhere, the offer is about a phone call.
distractors.B: "Be my guest" may sound like "it's on me", but no payment is mentioned here.
distractors.C: The opposite: she leaves the call to Mr. Tanaka and tells him who to ask for.

en.trap: An idiomatic reply answers the message before it: ask what was just offered, then translate it as "yes" or "no", never word for word.

evidence: I could call his office this morning if you like.
Ask for his assistant, Ms. Reyes.

questions.stem: Who most likely is Ms. Reyes?
options: A colleague at the accounting firm
A staff member at Whitfield Dental
An official at a tax agency

fr.rule: Mme Mensah parle du propriétaire de Whitfield Dental (« the owner », « his office ») et dit : « Ask for his assistant, Ms. Reyes ». Mme Reyes est donc l'assistante du client, et elle scanne ses relevés (« Ms. Reyes is scanning the statements now »).

distractors.A: Les collègues du cabinet sont Mme Mensah et M. Tanaka ; Mme Reyes est l'assistante de « his office », c'est-à-dire du client.
distractors.C: L'administration fiscale n'est citée nulle part comme interlocuteur de Mme Reyes ; elle prépare des documents pour le cabinet.
distractors.D: Les relevés viennent bien d'une banque, mais Mme Reyes les scanne depuis le bureau du propriétaire : elle n'y travaille pas.

fr.trap: Pour « Who most likely is… ? », cherche à qui appartient le possessif (« his assistant ») : il te dit pour qui travaille la personne.

en.rule: Ms. Mensah talks about the owner of Whitfield Dental ("the owner", "his office") and says "Ask for his assistant, Ms. Reyes". Ms. Reyes is therefore the client's assistant, and she is the one scanning his statements ("Ms. Reyes is scanning the statements now").

distractors.A: The firm's colleagues are Ms. Mensah and Mr. Tanaka; Ms. Reyes is the assistant at "his office", meaning the client's.
distractors.C: No tax agency is mentioned as Ms. Reyes's employer; she prepares documents for the firm.
distractors.D: The statements do come from a bank, but Ms. Reyes scans them from the owner's office: she does not work at the bank.

en.trap: For "Who most likely is...?", look at who the possessive belongs to ("his assistant"): it tells you who the person works for.

evidence: Ask for his assistant, Ms. Reyes.
Ms. Reyes is scanning the statements now

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the review?
options: To recommend a bank to other business owners
To explain how to open a business account

fr.rule: L'auteur dit vouloir partager son expérience avec d'autres propriétaires (« share my experience with other owners ») et termine par « I would recommend Linden Trust to any small business owner ». Le but est de recommander cette banque.

distractors.A: Il a regardé plusieurs options (« look at local options »), mais il ne parle que d'une seule banque.
distractors.B: Les nouveaux horaires ne sont qu'un détail du troisième paragraphe, et c'est la banque qui les annonce, pas lui.
distractors.D: Il dit que l'ouverture a pris un après-midi, sans décrire la procédure.

fr.trap: Pour un avis, le but se lit au début (pourquoi il écrit) et à la fin (la recommandation) ; un détail du milieu n'est qu'un distracteur.

en.rule: The writer says he wants to share his experience with other owners ("share my experience with other owners") and ends with "I would recommend Linden Trust to any small business owner". The purpose is to recommend this bank.

distractors.A: He looked at several options ("look at local options"), but he only reviews one bank.
distractors.B: The new hours are only a detail in the third paragraph, and it is the bank that announced them, not him.
distractors.D: He says the setup took one afternoon, but he does not describe the procedure.

en.trap: In a review, the purpose is at the start (why he writes) and at the end (the recommendation); a detail from the middle is just a distractor.

evidence: I wanted to share my experience with other owners.
I would recommend Linden Trust to any small business owner tired of high fees.

questions.stem: What is suggested about Mr. Alvarez?
options: He changed banks because of poor service.
He can easily maintain the minimum balance.
He visits the branch on Saturdays.

fr.rule: Le compte n'a pas de frais mensuels tant que le solde reste à 2 000 $ (« as long as I keep a balance of $2,000 »), et il ajoute « which is easy for me ». On en déduit qu'il garde sans effort le solde minimum.

distractors.A: Il dirige une société de fournitures pour boulangeries (« bakery supplies company »), pas une boulangerie.
distractors.B: Il est parti à cause de frais qui augmentaient (« monthly fees kept rising »), pas à cause du service.
distractors.D: La succursale n'ouvre pas le samedi (« is not open on Saturdays »).

fr.trap: Une question « suggested » se règle sur une phrase précise : ici « which is easy for me » ; ne retiens pas une option qui reprend seulement un mot du texte (« bakery »).

en.rule: The account has no monthly fee as long as the balance stays at $2,000 ("as long as I keep a balance of $2,000"), and he adds "which is easy for me". You can infer that he keeps the minimum balance without difficulty.

distractors.A: He runs a bakery supplies company, not a bakery.
distractors.B: He left because fees kept rising ("monthly fees kept rising"), not because of poor service.
distractors.D: The branch is closed on Saturdays ("is not open on Saturdays").

en.trap: A "suggested" question rests on one precise sentence: here "which is easy for me"; do not pick an option that merely reuses a word from the text ("bakery").

evidence: There is no monthly fee as long as I keep a balance of $2,000, which is easy for me.

questions.stem: What is NOT true about Linden Trust Bank?
options: Customers can deposit checks with a phone app.
An account manager gave a detailed explanation of fees.
It does not charge for wire transfers.
Its opening hours may be extended.

fr.rule: Le texte dit des virements : « Wire transfers are cheaper than at my previous bank, though still not free ». Ils coûtent moins cher, mais ne sont pas gratuits : l'option C est fausse. Les trois autres sont dans le texte : « the mobile app lets me deposit checks by photographing them », « spent almost an hour explaining the fee structure », « it plans to extend hours next spring ».

distractors.A: Vrai : l'application permet de déposer des chèques en les photographiant.
distractors.B: Vrai : Mme Abara a passé presque une heure à expliquer les frais.
distractors.D: Vrai : la banque prévoit d'allonger ses horaires au printemps prochain.

fr.trap: Pour « NOT true », retrouve dans le texte les trois options vraies ; celle qui reste est la réponse. Attention aux nuances (« cheaper » n'est pas « free »).

en.rule: About wire transfers the text says: "Wire transfers are cheaper than at my previous bank, though still not free". They cost less but are not free, so C is false. The other three are in the text: "the mobile app lets me deposit checks by photographing them", "spent almost an hour explaining the fee structure", "it plans to extend hours next spring".

distractors.A: True: the app lets customers deposit checks by photographing them.
distractors.B: True: Ms. Abara spent almost an hour explaining the fees.
distractors.D: True: the bank plans to extend its hours next spring.

en.trap: For "NOT true", find the three true options in the text; the one left is the answer. Watch for nuances ("cheaper" is not "free").

evidence: the mobile app lets me deposit checks by photographing them
spent almost an hour explaining the fee structure
it plans to extend hours next spring

questions.stem: What does Mr. Sato ask the delivery driver to bring?

fr.rule: Dans « Special instructions », M. Sato explique que son chariot élévateur est en réparation et demande : « the driver should bring a pallet jack » (un transpalette).

distractors.B: C'est le chariot élévateur de M. Sato (« Our forklift ») qui est en réparation : il demande justement un autre matériel.
distractors.C: Les séparateurs en carton sont commandés et « included with crate orders » ; il ne demande rien de plus.
distractors.D: Un acompte est mentionné dans la partie réservée au bureau, mais aucun reçu n'est demandé au chauffeur.

fr.trap: Dans un formulaire, lis les cases libres (« Special instructions ») : elles contiennent souvent la réponse à une question de détail.

en.rule: In "Special instructions", Mr. Sato explains that his forklift is being repaired and asks that "the driver should bring a pallet jack".

distractors.B: It is Mr. Sato's own forklift ("Our forklift") that is out for repairs: he is asking for different equipment.
distractors.C: The cardboard dividers are ordered and "included with crate orders"; he asks for nothing more.
distractors.D: A deposit appears in the office section, but the driver is not asked to bring any receipt.

en.trap: In a form, read the free-text boxes ("Special instructions"): they often hold the answer to a detail question.

evidence: so the driver should bring a pallet jack

questions.stem: What is suggested about Mr. Sato's order?
options: He will pick it up at the cooperative.
He will be asked to pay a deposit.
It was submitted after a deadline.
The cardboard dividers will be billed separately.

fr.rule: Il faut calculer : 30 caisses de pommes à 18 $ font 540 $, 25 caisses de poires à 22 $ font 550 $, soit 1 090 $. Or « Orders over $1,000 require a 25 percent deposit » : M. Sato devra verser un acompte, même si le texte ne le lui dit pas directement.

distractors.A: Le formulaire indique « Delivery to member farm » : la commande sera livrée chez lui.
distractors.C: Aucune date limite n'est mentionnée, et la commande est « Approved ».
distractors.D: Les séparateurs sont « included with crate orders » : ils ne sont pas facturés en plus.

fr.trap: Quand une règle porte sur un montant (« over $1,000 »), fais le calcul avec les quantités et les prix du formulaire avant de répondre.

en.rule: You have to calculate: 30 apple crates at $18 make $540, 25 pear crates at $22 make $550, a total of $1,090. Since "Orders over $1,000 require a 25 percent deposit", Mr. Sato will have to pay a deposit, even though the form never tells him so directly.

distractors.A: The form says "Delivery to member farm": the order will be delivered to him.
distractors.C: No deadline is mentioned, and the order is "Approved".
distractors.D: The dividers are "included with crate orders": they are not billed extra.

en.trap: When a rule depends on an amount ("over $1,000"), do the math with the quantities and prices on the form before answering.

evidence: Apple crates (40 lb) - quantity 30 - $18 per crate
Pear crates (40 lb) - quantity 25 - $22 per crate
Orders over $1,000 require a 25 percent deposit

questions.stem: What are the writers mainly discussing?
options: Where to buy a new sensor for the line
Whether to delay a customer's shipment
How to organize the night crew's break
How to get a stopped production line running again

fr.rule: Toute la conversation part de « Line 3 stopped about ten minutes ago » et finit par « Let's aim to restart by 8:00 » : ils cherchent comment remettre la ligne en marche (reset, capteur de rechange, installation).

distractors.A: Personne ne parle d'acheter un capteur : il y en a déjà un de rechange dans la réserve (« a spare in the supply cage »).
distractors.B: Au contraire : Mme Solberg dit que la commande doit partir à 14 h et qu'ils ne peuvent pas la manquer.
distractors.C: La pause de l'équipe de nuit n'est qu'un détail, évoqué à 7 h 10.

fr.trap: Pour l'idée générale d'un chat, cherche le problème posé au premier message et la solution du dernier ; un détail de milieu de conversation est un piège.

en.rule: The whole conversation starts with "Line 3 stopped about ten minutes ago" and ends with "Let's aim to restart by 8:00": they are working out how to get the line running again (reset, spare sensor, installation).

distractors.A: Nobody talks about buying a sensor: there is already a spare in the supply cage ("a spare in the supply cage").
distractors.B: On the contrary: Ms. Solberg says the order ships at 2:00 P.M. and they cannot miss it.
distractors.C: The night crew's break is only a detail, mentioned at 7:10.

en.trap: For the main idea of a chat, find the problem in the first message and the solution in the last; a detail from the middle is a trap.

evidence: Line 3 stopped about ten minutes ago.
Let's aim to restart by 8:00.

questions.stem: At 6:58 A.M., what does Mr. Qureshi most likely mean when he writes, "I'm on it"?
options: He is already using the spare sensor.
He is not sure the spare sensor is needed.
He wants someone else to check the numbers.
He will take care of comparing the part numbers.

fr.rule: Mme Solberg vient de lui demander « Can you compare the part numbers? ». « I'm on it » veut dire « je m'en occupe » : il va faire la comparaison.

distractors.A: Il n'a pas encore installé le capteur : à 7 h 09 il annonce seulement que la pièce convient.
distractors.B: Il ne doute pas : il accepte la tâche, et le capteur de rechange est bien utilisé ensuite.
distractors.C: C'est l'inverse : on lui demande de vérifier, et il répond qu'il le fait lui-même.

fr.trap: « I'm on it » = « je m'en charge ». Lis la demande juste avant : la réplique y répond directement.

en.rule: Ms. Solberg has just asked him "Can you compare the part numbers?". "I'm on it" means "I'll take care of it": he is going to do the comparison.

distractors.A: He has not installed the sensor yet: at 7:09 he only reports that the part fits.
distractors.B: He has no doubt: he accepts the task, and the spare is used afterward.
distractors.C: It is the opposite: he is asked to check, and he replies that he is doing it himself.

en.trap: "I'm on it" = "I'll handle it". Read the request just before: the reply answers it directly.

evidence: Can you compare the part numbers?

questions.stem: According to the chat, when will the Nordic Foods order ship?

fr.rule: Mme Solberg le dit directement : « an order for Nordic Foods that ships at 2:00 P.M. ».

distractors.A: 7 h correspond à peu près au moment où M. Wieczorek arrive, pas à un départ de commande.
distractors.B: 8 h est l'objectif de redémarrage de la ligne (« restart by 8:00 »), pas l'heure d'expédition.
distractors.D: 16 h n'apparaît pas dans la conversation.

fr.trap: Ne confonds pas les heures : note à quoi correspond chacune (redémarrage, expédition) avant de choisir.

en.rule: Ms. Solberg says it directly: "an order for Nordic Foods that ships at 2:00 P.M.".

distractors.A: About 7:00 is when Mr. Wieczorek arrives, not when an order ships.
distractors.B: 8:00 is the target time for restarting the line ("restart by 8:00"), not the shipping time.
distractors.D: 4:00 P.M. does not appear in the conversation.

en.trap: Do not mix up the times: note what each one refers to (restart, shipping) before choosing.

evidence: an order for Nordic Foods that ships at 2:00 P.M.

questions.stem: What can new clients receive without signing a contract?

fr.rule: La « free two-hour brand review » est offerte aux nouveaux clients, et « There is no obligation to hire us afterward » : aucun contrat n'est requis. Examiner le logo, le site et les réseaux sociaux, c'est évaluer l'image de marque.

distractors.B: Aucun tarif réduit n'est annoncé : les forfaits « start at $2,500 per month ».
distractors.C: La séance photo n'est offerte qu'à ceux qui signent un contrat de six mois (« Clients who sign a six-month contract »).
distractors.D: Le responsable de compte fait partie des forfaits payants (« Our packages… include a dedicated account manager »).

fr.trap: Une offre « gratuite » a souvent une condition : vérifie à qui elle s'adresse (tous les nouveaux clients, ou seulement ceux qui signent).

en.rule: The "free two-hour brand review" is offered to new clients, and "There is no obligation to hire us afterward": no contract is needed. Examining the logo, website and social media accounts means assessing the brand.

distractors.B: No reduced rate is announced: the packages "start at $2,500 per month".
distractors.C: The photo shoot is only for those who sign a six-month contract ("Clients who sign a six-month contract").
distractors.D: The account manager comes with the paid packages ("Our packages... include a dedicated account manager").

en.trap: A "free" offer often has a condition: check who it applies to (all new clients, or only those who sign).

evidence: new clients can book a free two-hour brand review
There is no obligation to hire us afterward.

questions.stem: What is implied about a client who signs a six-month contract?
options: The client will have to pay for the brand review.
The client will work with a different manager on each project.
The client must schedule the photo shoot in May.
The client will pay at least $15,000 in total.

fr.rule: Un contrat de six mois (« six-month contract ») avec des forfaits à partir de 2 500 $ par mois (« start at $2,500 per month ») : 6 x 2 500 = 15 000 $ au minimum.

distractors.A: La séance d'évaluation est gratuite (« free two-hour brand review »), y compris pour ceux qui signent ensuite.
distractors.B: Le client a un seul responsable « dedicated » qui suit chaque projet du début à la fin.
distractors.C: Le texte fixe une date limite pour signer (« before May 31 »), pas pour faire la séance photo.

fr.trap: Quand le texte donne une durée et un tarif mensuel, multiplie : l'inférence est un calcul, pas une information écrite.

en.rule: A six-month contract and packages starting at $2,500 per month ("start at $2,500 per month"): 6 x $2,500 = $15,000 at the very least.

distractors.A: The review is free ("free two-hour brand review"), even for those who sign afterward.
distractors.B: The client gets one "dedicated" manager who handles every project from start to finish.
distractors.C: The text sets a deadline for signing ("before May 31"), not for holding the photo shoot.

en.trap: When the text gives a length of time and a monthly price, multiply: the inference is a calculation, not a written fact.

evidence: Clients who sign a six-month contract before May 31
Our packages start at $2,500 per month

questions.stem: The word "handle" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to

fr.rule: « A dedicated account manager who will handle every project from start to finish » : le responsable s'occupe des projets, il les gère. « Handle » veut ici dire « manage ».

distractors.B: « touch » est le sens physique de « handle » (tenir dans les mains), qui ne va pas avec « project ».
distractors.C: « sell » est un autre sens possible (« handle a brand » = la vendre), mais le responsable ne vend pas les projets, il les suit.
distractors.D: « tolerate » correspond à « can't handle it » (supporter), sens étranger à cette phrase.

fr.trap: Pour un synonyme, remplace le mot par chaque option dans la phrase. Le sens physique (« toucher ») est un piège classique.

en.rule: "A dedicated account manager who will handle every project from start to finish": the manager takes care of the projects, he manages them. Here "handle" means "manage".

distractors.B: "touch" is the physical sense of "handle" (hold in the hands), which does not fit "project".
distractors.C: "sell" is another possible sense ("handle a brand" = sell it), but the manager does not sell the projects, he follows them.
distractors.D: "tolerate" matches "can't handle it" (bear), a sense that does not belong in this sentence.

en.trap: For a synonym question, put each option back into the sentence. The physical sense ("touch") is a classic trap.

evidence: a dedicated account manager who will handle every project from start to finish

questions.stem: At 8:36 A.M., what does Ms. Eze most likely mean when she writes, "No sweat"?
options: The extra tasks will not be a problem for her.
She does not want to work outdoors.
The seedlings will not need any watering.
It is too early in the day to begin.

fr.rule: Mme Whitaker vient de lui confier des tâches : mettre les plants à l'ombre dans l'heure et poser les étiquettes avant midi (« within an hour… price tags before noon »). « No sweat » veut dire « pas de problème » : elle accepte facilement.

distractors.B: Rien ne dit qu'elle refuse de travailler dehors ; elle vient de proposer de décharger (« I can take it »).
distractors.C: Sens littéral de « sweat » (transpiration) ou de l'arrosage : le message d'avant ne parle pas d'eau.
distractors.D: Elle est libre jusqu'à 11 h et accepte les tâches : elle ne dit pas qu'il est trop tôt.

fr.trap: Ne traduis pas une expression mot à mot (« sweat » = sueur) : cherche ce qui vient d'être demandé, puis ce qu'une réponse naturelle voudrait dire (« pas de souci »).

en.rule: Ms. Whitaker has just given her tasks: put the seedlings on the shaded tables within an hour and add price tags before noon ("within an hour... price tags before noon"). "No sweat" means "no problem": she accepts easily.

distractors.B: Nothing says she refuses to work outdoors; she has just offered to unload ("I can take it").
distractors.C: The literal sense of "sweat" or watering: the message before says nothing about water.
distractors.D: She is free until 11:00 and accepts the tasks: she does not say it is too early.

en.trap: Do not translate an expression word for word ("sweat"): look at what was just asked, then what a natural answer would mean ("no worries").

evidence: The seedlings need to be on the shaded tables within an hour of arriving, and they also need price tags before noon.

questions.stem: What will most likely happen at 10:00 A.M.?
options: Ms. Whitaker will unload the truck by herself.
Ms. Eze and Mr. Demir will unload the delivery together.
Mr. Demir will meet with a customer.
Ms. Whitaker will drive to Lakeview Nursery.

fr.rule: La livraison arrive à 10 h (« arrives at 10:00 »). Mme Eze s'est proposée pour décharger, et M. Demir, libre à 10 h (« I'm free at 10:00 »), la rejoint (« I'll meet you at the loading dock »). Les deux déchargeront donc le camion.

distractors.A: Mme Whitaker ne propose pas de décharger : Mme Eze s'en charge, rejointe par M. Demir.
distractors.C: Le rendez-vous client a été déplacé à 11 h 30 (« moved our consultation to 11:30 »).
distractors.D: Mme Whitaker ne se déplace nulle part : c'est le camion de Lakeview Nursery qui vient au magasin.

fr.trap: Pour « most likely happen », combine les messages dans l'ordre : le dernier changement (consultation déplacée) annule l'information du début.

en.rule: The delivery arrives at 10:00 ("arrives at 10:00"). Ms. Eze offered to unload, and Mr. Demir, who is free at 10:00 ("I'm free at 10:00"), will join her ("I'll meet you at the loading dock"). So the two of them will unload the truck.

distractors.A: Ms. Whitaker does not offer to unload: Ms. Eze takes it on, joined by Mr. Demir.
distractors.C: The customer meeting was moved to 11:30 ("moved our consultation to 11:30").
distractors.D: Ms. Whitaker goes nowhere: it is the Lakeview Nursery truck that comes to the store.

en.trap: For "most likely happen", combine the messages in order: the latest change (the consultation moved) cancels the earlier information.

evidence: The customer just moved our consultation to 11:30, so I'm free at 10:00.
I'll meet you at the loading dock, Adaeze.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the review?
options: To thank the pharmacists for their help
To object to a change in how refills are requested
To report a mistake on a prescription
To recommend the pharmacy's new app

fr.rule: Le deuxième paragraphe est le coeur de l'avis : « moved all refill requests to a new phone app and removed the old automated telephone line », puis « Please keep a telephone option ». Le client conteste un changement du système de renouvellement.

distractors.A: Les éloges du premier paragraphe sont réels, mais ils servent d'introduction (« That is why I am sorry to write a critical review »), pas de but.
distractors.C: L'erreur sur un formulaire a été corrigée par les pharmaciens il y a longtemps ; c'est un exemple de leur bon travail, pas l'objet de l'avis.
distractors.D: Il dit que l'application « often fails to load » et donne une étoile au système : il ne la recommande pas.

fr.trap: Le but d'un avis se lit dans ce qui motive la note et dans la demande finale, pas dans les compliments d'ouverture, qui servent souvent de leurre.

en.rule: The second paragraph is the heart of the review: "moved all refill requests to a new phone app and removed the old automated telephone line", then "Please keep a telephone option". The customer objects to a change in the refill system.

distractors.A: The praise in the first paragraph is genuine, but it is an introduction ("That is why I am sorry to write a critical review"), not the purpose.
distractors.C: The error on a form was corrected by the pharmacists long ago; it is an example of their good work, not the subject of the review.
distractors.D: He says the app "often fails to load" and gives the system one star: he does not recommend it.

en.trap: The purpose of a review is found in what justifies the rating and in the final request, not in the opening compliments, which are often a decoy.

evidence: Last month the pharmacy moved all refill requests to a new phone app and removed the old automated telephone line.
Please keep a telephone option for customers like me.

questions.stem: In the review, the word "managed" in the second paragraph is closest in meaning to

fr.rule: « managed to submit » suit « finally » et « often fails to load » : après des difficultés, il a réussi à envoyer sa demande. « succeeded » (réussir à) est le seul sens qui convient.

distractors.A: « directed » (diriger) est un autre sens de « manage », mais on ne dirige pas une demande de renouvellement.
distractors.C: « handled » (traiter, gérer) irait pour « managed the order », pas pour « managed to + verbe ».
distractors.D: « organized » (organiser) est un sens proche de « manage » pour un projet ou un planning, pas ici.

fr.trap: Dans « manage to + verbe », « manage » veut dire réussir, pas diriger. Remplace le mot par chaque option dans la phrase pour tester.

en.rule: "managed to submit" follows "finally" and "often fails to load": after difficulties, he succeeded in sending his request. "succeeded" is the only meaning that fits.

distractors.A: "directed" is another meaning of "manage", but you do not direct a refill request.
distractors.C: "handled" would suit "managed the order", not "managed to + verb".
distractors.D: "organized" is close to "manage" for a project or a schedule, not here.

en.trap: In "manage to + verb", "manage" means succeed, not direct. Put each option back into the sentence to test it.

evidence: When I finally managed to submit a refill on March 10

questions.stem: What does Mr. Holloway imply about the new app?
options: It was designed by the pharmacists.
It is available only to new customers.
It does not work well on every phone.
It can be used only on weekends.

fr.rule: Il écrit : « The app often fails to load on my older phone ». On en déduit que l'application ne fonctionne pas bien sur tous les téléphones.

distractors.A: Rien n'indique qui a conçu l'application ; il parle des pharmaciens seulement pour louer leur service.
distractors.B: Il est client depuis six ans et a lui-même essayé de l'utiliser : elle n'est pas réservée aux nouveaux clients.
distractors.D: Aucune restriction horaire n'est mentionnée ; le samedi apparaît seulement dans l'anecdote sur son médecin.

fr.trap: « Imply » : la réponse généralise une phrase précise (un téléphone ancien, donc pas tous les téléphones). Cherche cette phrase, ne rajoute aucun fait.

en.rule: He writes: "The app often fails to load on my older phone". You can infer that the app does not work well on every phone.

distractors.A: Nothing says who designed the app; he mentions the pharmacists only to praise their service.
distractors.B: He has been a customer for six years and has tried to use it himself: it is not limited to new customers.
distractors.D: No time restriction is mentioned; Saturday appears only in the story about his doctor.

en.trap: "Imply": the answer generalizes one precise sentence (an older phone, so not every phone). Find that sentence and do not add facts.

evidence: The app often fails to load on my older phone.

questions.stem: What most likely caused the delay that Mr. Holloway describes?
options: His doctor did not approve the refill.
A text-message alert was not sent.
The app did not accept his request.
The pharmacy was closed for two days.

fr.rule: L'avis décrit le retard : « nobody told me that the order was ready ». L'e-mail en donne la cause : le message texte censé prévenir le client était désactivé par erreur, jusqu'au 12 mars, donc au moment de sa commande du 10 mars.

distractors.A: Aucun des deux documents ne parle d'un refus de son médecin.
distractors.C: Il dit avoir réussi à envoyer sa demande le 10 mars (« managed to submit ») : le problème vient de l'absence de notification.
distractors.D: Aucune fermeture n'est mentionnée ; la pharmacie a préparé la commande, mais personne ne l'a prévenu.

fr.trap: Un retard décrit dans un document s'explique souvent dans l'autre. Repère le fait (« nobody told me »), puis cherche la cause dans la réponse.

en.rule: The review describes the delay: "nobody told me that the order was ready". The e-mail gives the cause: the text message meant to notify customers was switched off by mistake until March 12, which includes his March 10 order.

distractors.A: Neither document mentions his doctor refusing anything.
distractors.C: He says he managed to submit the request on March 10: the problem was the missing notification.
distractors.D: No closure is mentioned; the order was prepared, but nobody told him.

en.trap: A delay described in one document is often explained in the other. Find the fact ("nobody told me"), then look for the cause in the reply.

evidence: nobody told me that the order was ready, so I waited two extra days
The app is supposed to send a text message at that moment, but the feature was switched off by mistake during the first two weeks.

questions.stem: What does Ms. Ibarra say will happen on March 24?
options: The text-message feature will be repaired.
The automated refill line will be available again.
The new app will be removed.

fr.rule: L'e-mail dit : « Our automated refill line will return on March 24 ». « return » est reformulé par « be available again ».

distractors.A: La fonction de message a déjà été réparée le 12 mars (« We corrected the problem on March 12 »).
distractors.C: Les livraisons gratuites sont proposées, mais aucune date de début n'est donnée ; il faut présenter l'e-mail à un pharmacien.
distractors.D: L'application reste en service : la ligne téléphonique fonctionnera « alongside the app », à côté d'elle.

fr.trap: Plusieurs dates figurent dans le texte : associe chaque date à son événement avant de répondre, et méfie-toi des options qui déplacent un fait vers une autre date.

en.rule: The e-mail says: "Our automated refill line will return on March 24". "return" is paraphrased as "be available again".

distractors.A: The text-message feature was already repaired on March 12 ("We corrected the problem on March 12").
distractors.C: Free deliveries are offered, but no start date is given; he must show the e-mail to a pharmacist.
distractors.D: The app stays in service: the telephone line will work "alongside the app".

en.trap: Several dates appear in the text: match each date to its event before answering, and beware of options that move a fact to another date.

evidence: Our automated refill line will return on March 24 and will work alongside the app.

questions.stem: According to the job posting, what will the coordinator do?
options: Negotiate prices with the convention center

fr.rule: La liste des responsabilités contient : « assign booth space to participating companies ». « Companies » reprend « exhibitors » : c'est la réponse écrite.

distractors.B: La publicité du salon n'apparaît pas dans les tâches ; le coordinateur prépare un manuel pour les exposants.
distractors.C: La vente de billets n'est pas citée ; les exposants sont la clientèle de ce poste.
distractors.D: Le centre de congrès est un lieu, pas un partenaire avec lequel le coordinateur négocie.

fr.trap: Pour une question « what will the coordinator do », va droit à la liste « Responsibilities » : une tâche y est reformulée, les autres sont plausibles mais absentes.

en.rule: The list of responsibilities includes: "assign booth space to participating companies". The answer is written in the text.

distractors.B: Advertising for the show is not among the tasks; the coordinator prepares a manual for exhibitors.
distractors.C: Ticket sales are not mentioned; exhibitors are the clients of this job.
distractors.D: The convention center is a venue, not a partner the coordinator negotiates with.

en.trap: For a "what will the coordinator do" question, go straight to the "Responsibilities" list: one task is reworded, the others are plausible but absent.

evidence: assign booth space to participating companies

questions.stem: What is NOT mentioned as a benefit of the job?

fr.rule: Une seule phrase énumère les avantages : « health insurance, 15 days of paid vacation, and an annual training allowance ». Trois options la reformulent ; le parking n'y figure pas.

distractors.A: « Medical coverage » reformule « health insurance ».
distractors.C: « Time off with pay » reformule « 15 days of paid vacation ».
distractors.D: « Money for professional training » reformule « an annual training allowance ».

fr.trap: Question « NOT » : barre chaque option que tu retrouves dans le texte, même reformulée ; celle qui reste est la réponse.

en.rule: One sentence lists the benefits: "health insurance, 15 days of paid vacation, and an annual training allowance". Three options paraphrase it; parking is not in it.

distractors.A: "Medical coverage" paraphrases "health insurance".
distractors.C: "Time off with pay" paraphrases "15 days of paid vacation".
distractors.D: "Money for professional training" paraphrases "an annual training allowance".

en.trap: "NOT" question: cross out every option you find in the text, even reworded; the one left is the answer.

evidence: Benefits include health insurance, 15 days of paid vacation, and an annual training allowance.

questions.stem: Which skill that the job posting calls a plus does Mr. Banerjee have?

fr.rule: L'offre indique : « Knowledge of Spanish is a plus ». Dans sa lettre, M. Banerjee écrit : « I also speak fluent Spanish ». Il faut relier les deux documents.

distractors.A: Aucun diplôme n'est mentionné ni dans l'offre ni dans la lettre.
distractors.C: La vente au détail n'apparaît nulle part ; il travaille pour un fabricant de stands.
distractors.D: La vidéo n'est citée que pour l'entretien à distance, pas comme compétence.

fr.trap: Quand la question demande ce que « the posting calls a plus », trouve d'abord l'atout dans l'offre, puis vérifie dans la lettre que le candidat le possède.

en.rule: The posting says: "Knowledge of Spanish is a plus". In his letter, Mr. Banerjee writes: "I also speak fluent Spanish". You have to link the two documents.

distractors.A: No degree is mentioned in the posting or the letter.
distractors.C: Retail sales appear nowhere; he works for a company that builds booths.
distractors.D: Video is mentioned only for the remote interview, not as a skill.

en.trap: When the question asks what "the posting calls a plus", first find the plus in the posting, then check in the letter that the candidate has it.

evidence: Knowledge of Spanish is a plus.
I also speak fluent Spanish, which I use daily with clients in Latin America.

questions.stem: What is suggested about Mr. Banerjee?
options: He is already familiar with the Tidewater show.
He has applied for the position before.
He currently works for Tidewater Expo Group.
He has no experience with exhibitors.

fr.rule: Son employeur actuel construit « the exhibitor booths at your October show » et il a répondu à des exposants et livré au centre de congrès : il connaît donc déjà le salon Tidewater.

distractors.B: Rien n'indique une candidature antérieure.
distractors.C: Il travaille pour Kestrel Display Systems, un fournisseur de Tidewater Expo Group, pas pour Tidewater lui-même.
distractors.D: Il écrit au contraire : « I answered questions from exhibitors ».

fr.trap: Une déduction s'appuie sur un détail précis (ici, l'employeur construit les stands du salon). Évite les options qui contredisent la lettre ou ajoutent un fait.

en.rule: His current employer builds "the exhibitor booths at your October show" and he has dealt with exhibitors and deliveries at the convention center: he already knows the Tidewater show.

distractors.B: Nothing suggests an earlier application.
distractors.C: He works for Kestrel Display Systems, a supplier to Tidewater Expo Group, not for Tidewater itself.
distractors.D: He says the opposite: "I answered questions from exhibitors".

en.trap: An inference rests on one precise detail (here, his employer builds the show's booths). Avoid options that contradict the letter or add a fact.

evidence: the company that builds the exhibitor booths at your October show

questions.stem: What problem might the hiring schedule cause for Mr. Banerjee?
options: He may be unable to attend an interview in person.
He cannot begin work on September 15.
He will miss the application deadline.
He will not receive the training allowance.

fr.rule: L'offre fixe les entretiens aux 2 et 3 septembre. La lettre dit que M. Banerjee sera à l'étranger jusqu'au 5 septembre : il ne pourra sans doute pas venir en personne, d'où sa proposition d'une visioconférence.

distractors.B: Il écrit au contraire : « I would be free to start on September 15 as planned ».
distractors.C: Il écrit le 18 août ; la date limite de candidature est le 22 août.
distractors.D: La prime de formation n'est liée à aucun calendrier et il n'en est pas question dans la lettre.

fr.trap: Pour un problème de calendrier, place les dates des deux documents sur une même ligne du temps : le conflit apparaît quand deux dates se chevauchent.

en.rule: The posting sets interviews for September 2 and 3. The letter says Mr. Banerjee will be abroad until September 5, so he probably cannot come in person, which is why he offers a video call.

distractors.B: He says the opposite: "I would be free to start on September 15 as planned".
distractors.C: He writes on August 18; the application deadline is August 22.
distractors.D: The training allowance is not tied to any date and the letter never mentions it.

en.trap: For a scheduling problem, put the dates from both documents on one timeline: the conflict appears where two dates overlap.

evidence: Interviews will take place on September 2 and 3
I will be out of the country until September 5 for a trade fair in Valencia.

questions.stem: Why did Mr. Wren write to Ms. Park?
options: To cancel his registration for the workshop
To request a change to the program
To ask how to receive credit after missing part of a workshop
To suggest a topic for a future session

fr.rule: M. Wren explique qu'il devra partir après le déjeuner, puis demande : « Would it still be possible for me to receive a certificate if I miss the afternoon? ». Il veut savoir comment obtenir son attestation malgré une absence partielle.

distractors.A: Il reste inscrit : il dit attendre l'événement avec impatience et propose de rattraper la session manquée.
distractors.B: Il ne demande aucune modification du programme ; il le commente seulement.
distractors.D: Il parle d'un thème qui l'intéresse déjà au programme, pas d'un sujet futur.

fr.trap: Le but d'un e-mail se lit dans la demande précise, souvent au dernier paragraphe, pas seulement dans l'ouverture : ici, la question sur l'attestation.

en.rule: Mr. Wren explains that he will have to leave after lunch, then asks: "Would it still be possible for me to receive a certificate if I miss the afternoon?" He wants to know how to get credit despite missing part of the day.

distractors.A: He remains registered: he says he has been looking forward to the event and offers to make up the missed session.
distractors.B: He does not ask for any change to the program; he only comments on it.
distractors.D: He talks about a topic that is already on the program, not a future one.

en.trap: The purpose of an e-mail is found in its specific request, often in the last paragraph, not only in the opening: here, the question about the certificate.

evidence: Would it still be possible for me to receive a certificate if I miss the afternoon?

questions.stem: Which session will Mr. Wren miss?
options: Talking With Customers After a Loss

fr.rule: Dans l'e-mail, M. Wren doit partir « right after lunch ». Le programme place le déjeuner à 12 h 30, et la seule session qui suit est la quatrième, « Spotting Fraud Warning Signs », à 13 h 30.

distractors.A: La session 1 a lieu à 9 h 15, avant son départ.
distractors.B: La session 2, à 10 h 30, a lieu avant le déjeuner ; c'est même celle qui l'intéresse le plus.
distractors.C: La session 3 se tient à 11 h 30, avant le déjeuner.

fr.trap: Traduis l'indice de l'e-mail (« after lunch ») en heure grâce au programme, puis repère ce qui vient après.

en.rule: In the e-mail, Mr. Wren must leave "right after lunch". The schedule puts lunch at 12:30 P.M., and the only session afterward is Session 4, "Spotting Fraud Warning Signs", at 1:30 P.M.

distractors.A: Session 1 takes place at 9:15 A.M., before he leaves.
distractors.B: Session 2, at 10:30 A.M., is before lunch; it is even the one he cares about most.
distractors.C: Session 3 is at 11:30 A.M., before lunch.

en.trap: Turn the e-mail clue ("after lunch") into a time using the schedule, then find what comes after it.

evidence: I would need to leave right after lunch.
12:30 P.M. - Lunch (Atrium)
1:30 P.M. - Session 4: Spotting Fraud Warning Signs (Room 204) - Gareth Mbeki

questions.stem: What are participants asked to bring to the workshop?

fr.rule: Le programme demande : « Please bring a photo ID to collect your badge at check-in ». La réponse est écrite telle quelle.

distractors.A: Aucun formulaire d'inscription à imprimer n'est mentionné.
distractors.C: Aucun ordinateur n'est demandé.
distractors.D: Le parking est gratuit : « Parking in Lot C is free for workshop participants ».

fr.trap: Pour ce qu'on doit apporter, cherche les verbes « bring », « present », « show » : l'information est en général dans les consignes en bas du document.

en.rule: The schedule asks: "Please bring a photo ID to collect your badge at check-in". The answer is written word for word.

distractors.A: No registration form to print is mentioned.
distractors.C: No computer is requested.
distractors.D: Parking is free: "Parking in Lot C is free for workshop participants".

en.trap: For what participants must bring, look for "bring", "present", "show": the information is usually in the instructions at the bottom of the document.

evidence: Please bring a photo ID to collect your badge at check-in.

questions.stem: In the e-mail, the word "cover" in the second paragraph is closest in meaning to

fr.rule: « the workshop will cover the changes in detail » : un atelier traite un sujet, il l'aborde. « discuss » (aborder, traiter) convient.

distractors.B: « hide » (cacher) est un sens de « cover » pour un objet, pas pour un atelier.
distractors.C: « travel » vient de « cover a distance » (parcourir), qui ne s'applique pas à des changements.
distractors.D: « insure » est un piège lié au métier : « cover » veut dire assurer pour un contrat, mais un atelier n'assure pas des changements.

fr.trap: Dans une entreprise d'un secteur précis, le sens technique du mot (ici l'assurance) est souvent le piège : teste chaque option dans la phrase.

en.rule: "the workshop will cover the changes in detail": a workshop deals with a subject, it addresses it. "discuss" fits.

distractors.B: "hide" is a meaning of "cover" for an object, not for a workshop.
distractors.C: "travel" comes from "cover a distance", which does not apply to changes.
distractors.D: "insure" is a trap linked to the business: "cover" means to insure under a contract, but a workshop does not insure changes.

en.trap: In a company from a specific industry, the technical meaning of the word (here, insurance) is often the trap: test each option in the sentence.

evidence: I hope the workshop will cover the changes in detail

questions.stem: Who will lead the session that Mr. Wren is most interested in?

fr.rule: L'e-mail dit que M. Wren s'intéresse surtout à « the session on the new digital forms ». Dans le programme, la session 2, « New Digital Claim Forms », est animée par Yuki Hamasaki.

distractors.B: Gareth Mbeki anime les sessions 1 (tempêtes) et 4 (fraude).
distractors.C: Delphine Arnaud anime la session 3, sur la relation avec les clients.
distractors.D: Ainsley Park est la coordinatrice de la formation, destinataire de l'e-mail, pas une intervenante.

fr.trap: L'e-mail donne le sujet, le programme donne le nom : retrouve le titre dans la liste, puis lis le nom à côté.

en.rule: The e-mail says Mr. Wren is especially interested in "the session on the new digital forms". In the schedule, Session 2, "New Digital Claim Forms", is led by Yuki Hamasaki.

distractors.B: Gareth Mbeki leads Sessions 1 (storms) and 4 (fraud).
distractors.C: Delphine Arnaud leads Session 3, on talking with customers.
distractors.D: Ainsley Park is the training coordinator who receives the e-mail, not a speaker.

en.trap: The e-mail gives the topic, the schedule gives the name: find the title in the list, then read the name next to it.

evidence: I am especially interested in the session on the new digital forms
Session 2: New Digital Claim Forms (Room 204) - Yuki Hamasaki

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the brochure?
options: To announce a change in train service
To advertise apartments that are available to rent
To invite buyers to purchase new homes
To describe repairs to a city park

fr.rule: Dès la première phrase, la brochure annonce que l'immeuble « is now accepting applications for homes available from April 1 », et le deuxième paragraphe donne des loyers (« Monthly rents »). Elle sert donc à proposer des appartements à la location.

distractors.A: Les trains ne sont cités que comme un avantage de situation (la gare est à cinq minutes à pied) ; aucun changement de service n'est annoncé.
distractors.C: Les logements sont loués (« rents », « applications »), pas vendus : il n'est jamais question d'acheter.
distractors.D: Le parc Calder River apparaît seulement parce que les fenêtres donnent dessus ; aucun travaux n'est mentionné.

fr.trap: Pour une question de but, relie la première phrase au vocabulaire du texte (rents, applications) : les détails annexes (gare, parc) servent de distracteurs.

en.rule: In its first sentence the brochure says the building "is now accepting applications for homes available from April 1", and the second paragraph gives "Monthly rents". Its purpose is to offer apartments for rent.

distractors.A: Trains are only mentioned as a location advantage (the station is a five-minute walk away); no change in service is announced.
distractors.C: The homes are rented ("rents", "applications"), not sold: buying is never mentioned.
distractors.D: Calder River Park appears only because the windows face it; no repair work is mentioned.

en.trap: For a purpose question, link the first sentence to the text's vocabulary (rents, applications): side details (station, park) are used as distractors.

evidence: is now accepting applications for homes available from April 1
Monthly rents start at $1,150 for a studio

questions.stem: What is NOT mentioned as a feature of Willowmere Residences?

fr.rule: Une seule phrase prouve les trois options vraies : « a shared rooftop terrace, a bicycle storage room, and a fitness studio ». Aucune piscine n'apparaît dans la brochure.

distractors.B: Mentionnée : « a shared rooftop terrace ».
distractors.C: Mentionnée : « a bicycle storage room ».
distractors.D: Mentionnée : « a fitness studio open from 5:00 A.M. to 11:00 P.M. ».

fr.trap: Dans une question NOT, barre chaque option que tu retrouves dans le texte ; celle qui reste est la réponse. Ici, une seule liste contient les trois.

en.rule: One sentence proves the three true options: "a shared rooftop terrace, a bicycle storage room, and a fitness studio". No swimming pool appears anywhere in the brochure.

distractors.B: Mentioned: "a shared rooftop terrace".
distractors.C: Mentioned: "a bicycle storage room".
distractors.D: Mentioned: "a fitness studio open from 5:00 A.M. to 11:00 P.M.".

en.trap: In a NOT question, cross out each option you find in the text; the one left is the answer. Here a single list contains all three.

evidence: Residents also enjoy a shared rooftop terrace, a bicycle storage room, and a fitness studio open from 5:00 A.M. to 11:00 P.M.

questions.stem: The word "run" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to

fr.rule: « trains run to the city center every ten minutes » : les trains circulent, ils sont en service à cette fréquence. « Operate » est le sens qui convient pour un transport régulier.

distractors.A: « jog » (courir à petit trot) est le sens physique de « run » ; un train ne fait pas de jogging.
distractors.B: « manage » (diriger) existe pour « run a business », mais ici le sujet est « trains », pas une personne.
distractors.C: « flow » convient pour un liquide qui « runs » ; on ne dit pas qu'un train coule.

fr.trap: Remplace le mot par chaque option dans la phrase, en regardant son sujet : un mot très courant comme « run » a une dizaine de sens.

en.rule: "trains run to the city center every ten minutes": the trains travel, they are in service at that frequency. "Operate" fits a regular transport service.

distractors.A: "jog" is the physical meaning of "run"; a train does not jog.
distractors.B: "manage" fits "run a business", but here the subject is "trains", not a person.
distractors.C: "flow" suits a liquid that "runs"; you would not say a train flows.

en.trap: Put each option back into the sentence and look at the subject: a very common word like "run" has many meanings.

evidence: where trains run to the city center every ten minutes

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the e-mail?
options: To report a drop in holiday sales
To invite staff to a training session
To inform staff of a new way to handle returns
To ask staff to work extra shifts

fr.rule: Tout le message tourne autour d'un changement : « all returns will be handled at a new desk… instead of at the main registers ». Les horaires, la formation et le rappel de décembre dernier servent cette explication.

distractors.A: Le texte parle de clients partis l'an dernier, mais ne donne aucun chiffre de ventes et n'annonce aucune baisse.
distractors.B: La formation du 19 novembre est un détail du dispositif, pas le but du message : personne n'est invité à s'y inscrire.
distractors.D: Les deux associés du comptoir sont « assigned », mais aucun travail supplémentaire n'est demandé à l'équipe.

fr.trap: Quand plusieurs options reprennent un détail du texte, choisis celle qui résume l'ensemble du message, pas celle qui en cite une partie.

en.rule: The whole message is about one change: "all returns will be handled at a new desk… instead of at the main registers". The hours, the training and the reminder about last December all support this explanation.

distractors.A: Customers who left last year are mentioned, but no sales figures or drop are given.
distractors.B: The November 19 training is one detail of the plan, not the purpose of the message: nobody is invited to sign up for it.
distractors.D: Two associates are "assigned" to the desk, but no extra work is requested from the team.

en.trap: When several options repeat a detail from the text, pick the one that sums up the whole message, not one that quotes a part of it.

evidence: all returns will be handled at a new desk near the north entrance instead of at the main registers

questions.stem: At what time will the returns desk close each day?

fr.rule: Le texte donne l'amplitude : « open from 10:00 A.M. to 8:00 P.M. every day ». La fermeture est donc à 20 h.

distractors.A: 10 h est l'heure d'ouverture, pas de fermeture.
distractors.B: 6 h du soir n'apparaît pas dans le message.
distractors.C: Midi n'est cité nulle part ; l'ouverture est à 10 h.

fr.trap: Dans « from X to Y », lis bien quelle borne la question demande : le piège est souvent l'autre borne.

en.rule: The text gives the range: "open from 10:00 A.M. to 8:00 P.M. every day". The desk therefore closes at 8:00 P.M.

distractors.A: 10:00 A.M. is the opening time, not the closing time.
distractors.B: 6:00 P.M. does not appear in the message.
distractors.C: Noon is not mentioned anywhere; the desk opens at 10:00 A.M.

en.trap: In "from X to Y", check which end the question asks about: the trap is often the other end.

evidence: The desk will be open from 10:00 A.M. to 8:00 P.M. every day

questions.stem: What is NOT true about the new returns desk?
options: Returns without a receipt do not need approval.
It is located near the north entrance.
Its staff will be trained before it opens.
Gift receipts are accepted there for store credit.

fr.rule: Le message dit : « A supervisor will always be nearby to approve returns that have no receipt ». Un retour sans reçu a donc besoin d'une approbation : l'option A est fausse. Les trois autres sont prouvées par les passages cités.

distractors.B: Vrai : « a new desk near the north entrance ».
distractors.C: Vrai : la formation a lieu le jeudi 19 novembre, et le comptoir ouvre le lundi 23 (« Starting Monday, November 23 »).
distractors.D: Vrai : « Gift receipts will be accepted there for store credit only ».

fr.trap: Dans une question NOT TRUE, une option peut être contredite par une phrase éloignée des autres : vérifie chaque option, y compris celle qui te semble « logique ».

en.rule: The message says: "A supervisor will always be nearby to approve returns that have no receipt". A return without a receipt therefore needs approval, so option A is false. The other three are proved by the quoted passages.

distractors.B: True: "a new desk near the north entrance".
distractors.C: True: the training is on Thursday, November 19, and the desk opens on Monday, November 23 ("Starting Monday, November 23").
distractors.D: True: "Gift receipts will be accepted there for store credit only".

en.trap: In a NOT TRUE question, an option may be contradicted by a sentence far from the others: check every option, even the one that seems "logical".

evidence: a new desk near the north entrance
will train the associates who are assigned to the desk on Thursday, November 19
Gift receipts will be accepted there for store credit only.

questions.stem: What is suggested about last December?
options: The store closed early on some days.
A returns desk was already in use.
The store lost some sales because of long lines.

fr.rule: Le texte dit que la file de retours « stretched past the shoe department » et que « several customers left without finishing their purchases ». On en déduit que l'attente a fait perdre des ventes au magasin.

distractors.A: Aucune fermeture anticipée n'est mentionnée.
distractors.B: Le comptoir est « new » et remplace les caisses principales : il n'existait pas l'an dernier.
distractors.D: Le rayon chaussures sert seulement de repère pour la longueur de la file ; il n'est pas question de le déplacer.

fr.trap: Une inférence s'appuie sur une phrase précise : ici, des clients partis sans finir leurs achats = des ventes perdues.

en.rule: The text says the returns line "stretched past the shoe department" and "several customers left without finishing their purchases". You can infer that the wait cost the store some sales.

distractors.A: No early closing is mentioned.
distractors.B: The desk is "new" and replaces the main registers: it did not exist last year.
distractors.D: The shoe department is only a landmark for the length of the line; moving it is never mentioned.

en.trap: An inference rests on one precise sentence: here, customers leaving without finishing their purchases = lost sales.

evidence: the returns line stretched past the shoe department and several customers left without finishing their purchases

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the letter?
options: To request payment for finished work
To inform a client of a new completion date
To propose adding a room to the project
To thank a client for choosing the company

fr.rule: M. Almeida écrit « to update you on the renovation » puis explique que les travaux seront finis le 11 décembre « rather than on November 30, the date in our contract ». Le but est d'annoncer une nouvelle date de fin.

distractors.A: Aucune facture ni demande de paiement : les travaux ne sont pas terminés.
distractors.C: Aucune nouvelle pièce n'est proposée ; il s'agit des salles de soins déjà prévues.
distractors.D: Il n'y a aucun remerciement dans la lettre.

fr.trap: Le but d'une lettre se trouve dans sa première phrase (« update you on… ») et se précise dans le premier paragraphe ; vérifie-le avec la date ou le chiffre qui change.

en.rule: Mr. Almeida writes "to update you on the renovation" and then explains that the work will be completed on December 11, "rather than on November 30, the date in our contract". The purpose is to announce a new completion date.

distractors.A: There is no invoice or request for payment: the work is not finished.
distractors.C: No new room is proposed; the letter is about the treatment rooms already planned.
distractors.D: There is no thanks anywhere in the letter.

en.trap: The purpose of a letter is in its first sentence ("update you on…") and becomes clear in the first paragraph; check it against the date or figure that changes.

evidence: the work will be completed on Friday, December 11, rather than on November 30, the date in our contract

questions.stem: By how many days will the work finish later than the date in the contract?

fr.rule: Le contrat prévoyait le 30 novembre et la nouvelle date est le 11 décembre : 1 jour jusqu'au 1er décembre + 10 jours = 11 jours.

distractors.B: Sept jours séparent l'arrivée des cloisons (4 décembre) de la fin des travaux (11 décembre), pas la date du contrat de la nouvelle date.
distractors.C: Quatorze jours n'apparaissent pas dans le texte ; ce n'est pas l'écart entre les deux dates.
distractors.D: Quatre jours séparent le 30 novembre du 4 décembre, date d'arrivée des cloisons : ce n'est pas le retard des travaux.

fr.trap: Pour un calcul de dates, repère les deux dates que la question compare (ici contrat et nouvelle fin) ; les autres dates du texte sont des pièges.

en.rule: The contract date was November 30 and the new date is December 11: 1 day to reach December 1, plus 10 days, makes 11 days.

distractors.B: Seven days is the gap between the partitions' arrival (December 4) and the end of the work (December 11), not between the contract date and the new date.
distractors.C: Fourteen days does not appear in the text; it is not the gap between the two dates.
distractors.D: Four days is the gap between November 30 and December 4, when the partitions arrive: it is not the delay of the work.

en.trap: For a date calculation, find the two dates the question compares (here contract and new finish); the other dates in the text are traps.

evidence: the work will be completed on Friday, December 11, rather than on November 30, the date in our contract

questions.stem: The word "cover" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to

fr.rule: « we will cover the cost of the extra shifts ourselves » : l'entreprise paiera ces heures, sans les facturer. « Pay for » est le sens qui va avec « the cost ».

distractors.B: « hide » (cacher) est un sens de « cover », mais on ne cache pas un coût.
distractors.C: « protect » (couvrir pour protéger) ne va pas avec « the cost » : rien n'est mis à l'abri.
distractors.D: « travel » existe pour « cover 10 miles », mais n'a aucun rapport avec un coût.

fr.trap: Un mot à plusieurs sens se tranche avec son complément : « cover » + « the cost » = payer.

en.rule: "we will cover the cost of the extra shifts ourselves": the company will pay for these hours without billing them. "Pay for" is the meaning that goes with "the cost".

distractors.B: "hide" is a meaning of "cover", but you do not hide a cost.
distractors.C: "protect" (cover to keep safe) does not go with "the cost": nothing is being sheltered.
distractors.D: "travel" exists in "cover 10 miles", but has nothing to do with a cost.

en.trap: A word with several meanings is settled by its object: "cover" + "the cost" = pay.

evidence: we will cover the cost of the extra shifts ourselves

questions.stem: In which of the positions marked [1], [2], [3], and [4] does the following sentence best belong? "That is two weeks later than the supplier first promised."

fr.rule: « That » renvoie à une date de livraison : seule la phrase « The custom glass partitions… will now arrive on December 4 » la donne, et « That is two weeks later than the supplier first promised » la commente juste après.

distractors.A: En [1], aucune date de livraison n'a encore été donnée : « That » n'aurait pas de référent.
distractors.C: En [3], la phrase précédente parle de la fin des travaux (11 décembre) ; le fournisseur n'a rien promis pour la fin des travaux, et l'écart avec le 30 novembre est de 11 jours, pas de deux semaines.
distractors.D: En [4], la phrase précédente porte sur les équipes du samedi et les coûts ; rien ne renvoie à une promesse du fournisseur.

fr.trap: Pour une insertion, repère le mot de liaison (« That », « this ») et cherche juste avant la phrase à laquelle il renvoie, puis vérifie que la suite se raccorde encore.

en.rule: "That" refers to a delivery date: only the sentence "The custom glass partitions… will now arrive on December 4" gives one, and "That is two weeks later than the supplier first promised" comments on it right after.

distractors.A: At [1], no delivery date has been given yet: "That" would have no referent.
distractors.C: At [3], the previous sentence is about the end of the work (December 11); the supplier promised nothing about that, and the gap from November 30 is 11 days, not two weeks.
distractors.D: At [4], the previous sentence is about Saturday shifts and costs; nothing refers to a supplier's promise.

en.trap: For sentence insertion, spot the link word ("That", "this") and look just before for the sentence it points to, then check that what follows still connects.

evidence: The custom glass partitions for the treatment rooms will now arrive on December 4.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the report?
options: To summarize the results of the summer tourist season
To announce the opening of new boat tours
To compare hotel prices in the region
To ask for money to build a parking lot

fr.rule: La première phrase le dit : « This report summarizes visitor numbers and survey results for the summer season ». Les chiffres et l'enquête qui suivent détaillent ce bilan.

distractors.B: Les excursions en bateau existent déjà : elles « remained the most popular activity ».
distractors.C: Les hôtels ne sont cités que pour leur taux d'occupation ; aucun prix n'est comparé.
distractors.D: Le conseil prévoit une navette et des cartes, pas un nouveau parking, et ne demande aucun financement.

fr.trap: Dans un rapport, la phrase d'ouverture annonce l'objet ; les mesures proposées à la fin sont des conséquences, pas le but.

en.rule: The first sentence says it: "This report summarizes visitor numbers and survey results for the summer season". The figures and the survey that follow detail this review.

distractors.B: The boat tours already exist: they "remained the most popular activity".
distractors.C: Hotels are only mentioned for their occupancy rate; no prices are compared.
distractors.D: The board plans a shuttle and maps, not a new parking lot, and asks for no funding.

en.trap: In a report, the opening sentence states its subject; measures proposed at the end are consequences, not the purpose.

evidence: This report summarizes visitor numbers and survey results for the summer season, from June to August.

questions.stem: The word "ease" in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to

fr.rule: « To ease congestion » : la navette doit diminuer l'encombrement du port, donc le « réduire ». On soulage un problème en le rendant moins fort.

distractors.A: « comfort » (réconforter) vient du sens « ease someone's pain » ; on ne réconforte pas un embouteillage.
distractors.B: « loosen » (desserrer) s'applique à une corde ou une règle ; on ne desserre pas un encombrement, on le diminue.
distractors.C: « simplify » rappelle « make easier » ; mais la navette ne rend pas l'encombrement plus simple, elle le diminue.

fr.trap: Avec un mot abstrait, teste chaque synonyme avec le complément exact (« congestion ») : seul celui qui reste naturel est correct.

en.rule: "To ease congestion": the shuttle should lessen the crowding at the harbor, that is, "reduce" it. You ease a problem by making it less strong.

distractors.A: "comfort" comes from "ease someone's pain"; you do not comfort traffic congestion.
distractors.B: "loosen" suits a rope or a rule; you do not loosen congestion, you lessen it.
distractors.C: "simplify" echoes "make easier", but the shuttle does not make congestion simpler, it makes it smaller.

en.trap: With an abstract word, test each synonym with the exact object ("congestion"): only the one that stays natural is correct.

evidence: To ease congestion, the board plans to open a shuttle service from the Eastfield lot next June.

questions.stem: In which of the positions marked [1], [2], [3], and [4] does the following sentence best belong? "Some visitors said they gave up and left for the neighboring town instead."

fr.rule: « gave up » suppose un problème rencontré juste avant : le stationnement saturé (« the lots fill up before 10:00 A.M. »). La phrase prépare ensuite la réponse du conseil, « To ease congestion, the board plans… ».

distractors.A: En [1], on vient de lire que 86 % des visiteurs sont satisfaits : personne n'a de raison de « give up ».
distractors.B: En [2], on loue les excursions et le marché nocturne ; abandonner n'a aucun lien avec ces éloges.
distractors.D: En [4], la phrase précédente propose des cartes de parkings gratuits ; la phrase insérée viendrait après la solution, et non après le problème.

fr.trap: Repère dans la phrase à insérer l'événement qu'elle suppose (ici un problème) et place-la juste après sa mention, avant la solution.

en.rule: "gave up" assumes a problem met just before: the full parking ("the lots fill up before 10:00 A.M."). The sentence then leads into the board's response, "To ease congestion, the board plans…".

distractors.A: At [1], we have just read that 86 percent of visitors are satisfied: nobody has a reason to "give up".
distractors.B: At [2], the boat tours and the night market are praised; giving up has no link with this praise.
distractors.D: At [4], the previous sentence offers maps of free parking; the inserted sentence would come after the solution, not after the problem.

en.trap: Find the event the sentence to insert assumes (here a problem) and place it right after that event, before the solution.

evidence: The most common complaint was parking near the harbor, where the lots fill up before 10:00 A.M. on weekends.

questions.stem: What problem does Ms. Rao report?
options: A file takes a long time to open.

fr.rule: Mme Rao répond que le problème vient du fichier de budget : « It takes about five minutes to open ». Un fichier long à ouvrir, c'est ce que dit l'option D.

distractors.A: L'ordinateur fonctionne : il est seulement lent avec un fichier.
distractors.B: Aucun mot de passe n'est évoqué.
distractors.C: L'appel client de 16 h est maintenu : elle en a besoin pour le fichier.

fr.trap: Pour une question de détail dans un chat, retrouve la réplique de la personne et reformule-la : « takes five minutes to open » = « takes a long time to open ».

en.rule: Ms. Rao answers that the problem is with the budget file: "It takes about five minutes to open". A file that takes a long time to open is option D.

distractors.A: The laptop works: it is only slow with one file.
distractors.B: No password is mentioned.
distractors.C: The 4:00 P.M. client call is still on: she needs the file for it.

en.trap: For a detail question in a chat, find the person's line and paraphrase it: "takes five minutes to open" = "takes a long time to open".

evidence: It takes about five minutes to open, and then the program often freezes.

questions.stem: At 2:12 P.M., what does Ms. Rao most likely mean when she writes, "Sounds like a plan"?
options: She thinks the repair will be complicated.
She agrees to bring her laptop to the help desk.
She has made a schedule for the client call.

fr.rule: M. Nasser vient de proposer : « Bring it to the help desk on the second floor and I'll start right away ». « Sounds like a plan » veut dire « d'accord, ça me convient » ; elle ajoute d'ailleurs « I'll be there in ten minutes ».

distractors.A: Elle ne parle pas de difficulté : l'expression est une approbation.
distractors.C: « plan » désigne ici la proposition de M. Nasser, pas un programme préparé pour l'appel.
distractors.D: Elle accepte M. Nasser et va le retrouver : elle ne demande personne d'autre.

fr.trap: Une expression idiomatique se lit d'après le message précédent : cherche la proposition ou la question à laquelle elle répond.

en.rule: Mr. Nasser has just suggested: "Bring it to the help desk on the second floor and I'll start right away". "Sounds like a plan" means "that works for me"; she adds "I'll be there in ten minutes".

distractors.A: She does not mention any difficulty: the expression is an approval.
distractors.C: "plan" refers to Mr. Nasser's suggestion, not to a schedule prepared for the call.
distractors.D: She accepts Mr. Nasser and is going to meet him: she does not ask for anyone else.

en.trap: An idiom is read from the previous message: look for the suggestion or question it answers.

evidence: Bring it to the help desk on the second floor and I'll start right away.

questions.stem: What is suggested about Ms. Rao's laptop?
options: It will be replaced next week.
It is too old to run the budget program.
Its security software is not up to date.
It was lent to her by the help desk.

fr.rule: M. Pritchard demande de mettre à jour l'antivirus et précise « The patch is due this week » : la mise à jour n'est donc pas encore faite, le logiciel de sécurité n'est pas à jour.

distractors.A: Aucun remplacement n'est évoqué : on compresse un fichier et on nettoie l'ordinateur.
distractors.B: Le programme s'ouvre, très lentement : le problème est la taille du fichier (480 MB), pas l'âge de la machine.
distractors.D: C'est « your laptop » : rien n'indique qu'il appartient au service informatique.

fr.trap: Une inférence se tire d'une réplique précise, ici la demande de mise à jour : si elle est demandée, c'est qu'elle n'est pas faite.

en.rule: Mr. Pritchard asks for the antivirus software to be updated and adds "The patch is due this week": the update has not been done yet, so the security software is not up to date.

distractors.A: No replacement is mentioned: a file is compressed and the computer is cleaned up.
distractors.B: The program opens, very slowly: the problem is the file size (480 MB), not the age of the machine.
distractors.D: It is "your laptop": nothing suggests it belongs to the help desk.

en.trap: An inference comes from one precise line, here the update request: if it is requested, it has not been done.

evidence: can you also update the antivirus software on that laptop? The patch is due this week.

questions.stem: What is NOT stated about the work Mr. Nasser will do on the laptop?
options: He will replace the hard drive.
He will need about an hour.
He will compress a large file.
He will remove old temporary files.

fr.rule: M. Nasser propose de compresser le fichier et de garder l'ordinateur « about an hour », puis de nettoyer les fichiers temporaires. Il ne parle jamais de changer le disque dur.

distractors.B: Dit : « I'd need to keep your laptop for about an hour ».
distractors.C: Dit : « I can compress it », à propos du fichier de 480 MB.
distractors.D: Dit : « I'll also clear out her old temporary files ».

fr.trap: Dans un chat, les trois options vraies sont éparpillées sur plusieurs répliques : retrouve-les une à une et garde celle qui n'a aucune trace.

en.rule: Mr. Nasser offers to compress the file and keep the laptop for "about an hour", then to clear temporary files. He never mentions changing the hard drive.

distractors.B: Stated: "I'd need to keep your laptop for about an hour".
distractors.C: Stated: "I can compress it", about the 480 MB file.
distractors.D: Stated: "I'll also clear out her old temporary files".

en.trap: In a chat, the three true options are spread over several lines: find them one by one and keep the one with no trace.

evidence: I can compress it, but I'd need to keep your laptop for about an hour.
I'll also clear out her old temporary files

questions.stem: What is indicated about the 3-D model?
options: It is included in the Design Package.
It is free for Full Service clients.
It is completed within two weeks.
It is not offered with the Concept Package.

fr.rule: La brochure réserve le modèle 3D aux clients qui choisissent « the Design Package or the Full Service Package ». Le Concept Package n'est pas cité : le modèle n'y est donc pas proposé.

distractors.A: Le modèle est une option payante (« may add… for $400 ») ; il n'est pas compris dans le Design Package.
distractors.B: Le texte dit « for $400 » pour les deux formules : aucune gratuité pour le Full Service.
distractors.C: « Within two weeks » est le délai du Concept Package ; la brochure ne donne aucun délai pour le modèle 3D.

fr.trap: Quand une option est réservée à certaines formules, la bonne réponse se déduit de celles qui ne sont pas citées : relis la liste complète.

en.rule: The brochure reserves the 3-D model for clients who choose "the Design Package or the Full Service Package". The Concept Package is not named, so the model is not offered with it.

distractors.A: The model is a paid option ("may add... for $400"); it is not included in the Design Package.
distractors.B: The text says "for $400" for both packages: nothing is free for Full Service clients.
distractors.C: "Within two weeks" is the Concept Package's time frame; the brochure gives no time frame for the 3-D model.

en.trap: When an option is limited to certain packages, the right answer comes from the ones that are not named: reread the whole list.

evidence: Clients who choose the Design Package or the Full Service Package may add a 3-D model of the finished project for $400.

questions.stem: In the brochure, the word "holds" in the last paragraph is closest in meaning to

fr.rule: « A deposit... holds your start date » : le dépôt bloque la date de début pour toi, donc il la réserve (« reserves »).

distractors.B: « grips » est le sens physique de « hold » (tenir dans la main) ; un dépôt ne tient rien dans la main.
distractors.C: « contains » est le sens de « hold » pour un récipient (« the tank holds 50 liters ») ; une somme d'argent ne contient pas une date.
distractors.D: « organizes » est le sens de « hold » pour un événement (« hold a meeting ») ; le dépôt n'organise pas la date, il la garde pour toi.

fr.trap: Remplace le mot par chaque option dans la phrase : seule la version qui garde le sens du texte est la bonne, pas celle qui est valable dans une autre phrase.

en.rule: "A deposit... holds your start date": the deposit keeps the start date for you, so it reserves it.

distractors.B: "grips" is the physical meaning of "hold" (in your hand); a deposit does not grip anything.
distractors.C: "contains" is the meaning of "hold" for a container ("the tank holds 50 liters"); money does not contain a date.
distractors.D: "organizes" is the meaning of "hold" for an event ("hold a meeting"); the deposit does not organize the date, it keeps it for you.

en.trap: Put each option back into the sentence: only the one that keeps the text's meaning is right, not the one that works in another sentence.

evidence: covers the first site visit and holds your start date
